evidence: Hopeton Overton Brown began hanging around King Tubby's studio, drawn in by his father's work in electronics repair, and was hired as an assistant, winding transformer coils before moving up to mixing in the mid-1970s. Bunny Lee is the source of his stage name: seeing his technical ability, Lee remarked to King Tubby, 'this little boy must be a scientist,' and the name stuck (Wikipedia's article on Scientist).

later.title: Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires

trackPair.whatToListenFor: There is no shared record to compare here: this is an origin story, not a sound Lee handed down. Listen instead to how far the name travelled. 'Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires' plays the mixing desk like an instrument, sounds swooping and vanishing as if by an actual scientist at work, the same joke Bunny Lee made off the cuff years before it became one of the most recognisable names in dub.

explanation: The dub mixer Scientist wasn't born with that name. Producer Bunny Lee gave it to him in an offhand remark to King Tubby, admiring how technically skilled the teenage assistant was: 'this little boy must be a scientist.' This is a naming story, not a teacher's: Scientist's real teacher was King Tubby, who has his own connections to him on the map. Bunny Lee's part was smaller, but documented and specific, so it gets its own line.
